a: daiva a. (vī f.) [devādāgataḥ aṇ] Relating to gods, caused by or coming from gods, divine, celestial; saṃskṛtaṃ nāma daivī vāganvākhyātā maharṣibhiḥ Kāv. 1. 33; daivīnāṃ mānuṣīṇāṃ ca pratihartā tvamāpadāṃ R. 1. 60; Y. 2. 235; Bg. 4. 25, 9. 13, 16. 3; Ms. 3. 75. — vaḥ (i. e. vivāhaḥ) One of the eight forms of marriage, that in which the daughter is given away at a sacrifice to the officiating priest; yajñasya ṛtvije daivaḥ Y. 1. 59; (for the eight forms of marriage see udvāha or Ms. 3. 21). — vaṃ 1 Fate, destiny, luck, fortune; daivamavidvāṃsaḥ pramāṇayaṃti Mu. 3; vinā puruṣakāreṇa daivamatra na sidhyati ‘God helps those who help  themselves’; daivaṃ nihatya kuru pauruṣama tmaśaktyā Pt. 1. 361. (daivāt by chance, luckily, accidentally). 2 A god, deity. 3 A religious rite or offering, an oblation to gods. 4 A kind of Śrāddha ceremony. 5 Parts of the hands sacred to the gods, i. e. the tips of the fingers; cf. Ms. 2. 59. — vī A woman married according to the form of marriage called daiva q. v. above.
